name: The Port City of Goldraft
description: Goldraft City, once a great port city of the Empire, now struggles amidst the Republic’s economic hurdles. While bronze domes and spires stretch toward the heavens, echoing past glories, the city has clearly lost its luster. During the day, one can see the enduring stalls of the merchants and the many ships docking, as people strive to make a living. Myriad sails and flags wave, each symbolizing their captain’s ambition. At the city’s heart, an ancient lighthouse emits a haunting green light, which local whispers say guides more than mere ships. Yet it is at dawn that the bustling port truly comes alive, with adventurers weaving through streets filled with diverse inns and boisterous taverns bustling with captains, merchants, buccaneers, adventurers, and locals. Their nightly festivities paint a facade of joy, immersed in ale, dice games, and loud music. Yet danger looms. A deadly plague, marked by black spots and hallucinations, spreads from the docks, sparing no one; even mighty pirate captains fall victim to it. Rumors trace its origin to a cursed island or perhaps the chants of dark cultists. Locals accuse sailors of introducing the disease, while sailors deem the city cursed. Many captains are now beginning to avoid the port of Goldraft, risking the city’s primary trade. As tensions rise, famine may soon join the plague as another impending peril. Amidst this situation, a local legend speaks of a place where a sick man can potentially find a cure: the Shadow Harbor’s Market. Stories tell of a ghostly market where souls are traded, overseen by malevolent faeries. This elusive place appears only on full moons as an inconspicuous door within one of the city’s alleys, always in a different location. Rumor says that an ancient pact binds this market to Goldraft. Still, Goldraft’s allure remains. Adventurers flock here to brave treacherous waters, pursue pirates, uncover hidden treasures, and safeguard merchant ships. Despite its challenges, Goldraft City continues to attract those eager to forge their own sagas.
